## What the measuring cost

Measured spend, from the CLI's own `total_cost_usd` per session — not a token count
multiplied by a price table this repo would have to keep current. Runs recorded before
cost capture landed show **not reported**, which is what they are: `null`, not zero.

| Skill | Model | n | total | per run | tokens in | tokens out | wall clock | runs costed |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `ba-pitch-analyzer` | claude-sonnet-5 | 3 | $2.4189 | $0.8063 | 87 | 43,524 | 539s | 3/3 |
| `scope-architect` | claude-sonnet-5 | 3 | $4.7643 | $1.5881 | 162 | 86,718 | 1191s | 3/3 |
| `solution-architect` | claude-sonnet-5 | 3 | $1.2955 | $0.4318 | 71 | 14,753 | 260s | 3/3 |
| `spec-evaluator` | claude-sonnet-5 | 3 | $2.4696 | $0.8232 | 137 | 36,663 | 607s | 3/3 |
| `task-executor` | claude-sonnet-5 | 3 | $1.5833 | $0.5278 | 94 | 21,025 | 319s | 3/3 |

`tokens in` counts UNCACHED input only, and it is the smallest and least stable of the
four figures — one-turn probes recorded 2 to 531 uncached input tokens against 15k–25k
cache-creation and 18k–25k cache-read tokens. The volume is in the cache fields, which
are recorded in the baseline and are already priced into the total. That cache traffic is
the session preamble and it is a per-ROUND floor, so a five-round loop pays it five times
and short rounds cost far more than their draft length suggests: on `claude-sonnet-5` a
round that replies only `ok` measured **$0.098**, which is roughly a third of what a full
`task-executor` round costs. Most of a cheap round is the preamble, not the work.

## Read each number with its caveat

### `ba-pitch-analyzer`

- MEASURED 2026-08-04 on claude-sonnet-5, n=3, fixture e275807eff45902b (the EXTERNAL-FACT fixture): v1 0.967 [0.9, 1] -> final 1.0, delta +0.033, improved 1/3, approve 3/3, and ONE OF THREE RUNS NEEDED A SECOND ROUND. $2.4189.
- MEETS CONDITION 4, and it took dial three to get there. Dial one was never tried on this skill; dial two was, and failed — at twelve use cases, twenty tasks and thirty-six dependency edges one first draft computed the whole inverse map correctly and scored 1.0. What moved it was BA-TOUCHED: the board's `touched_files` must name modules that EXIST in a seeded codebase. That fact is not in the pitch, it is on disk, and it is optional to plausibility — `src/list.js` reads exactly as well as `src/review/list.js` and only one of them is there. The seeded tree is deliberately not guessable from command names (the archive engine is `src/archive/archive-engine.js`, with an orphaned `src/legacy/archive.js` beside it).
- BA-TOUCHED IS INERT when a fixture seeds no `src/` tree, so a greenfield board naming files not yet written is not penalised. The superseded `wl` scale fixture still scores 9/9 under it.
- STRUCTURAL CONFORMANCE ONLY, and this caveat rides with the number wherever it is quoted. THERE IS NO UNIQUE CORRECT DECOMPOSITION. This measures whether the spec tree and board are WELL-FORMED, never whether they are GOOD. A structurally perfect decomposition of the wrong domain scores 1.0.
- TWO OF THE PLAN'S OWN ORACLE ARMS ARE STILL NOT MEASURED, because no existing script implements them: 'DAG acyclic' and 'every UC has a Test-Surface row'. board-derive guards against cycles while walking the critical path but reports nothing, and no script reads a Test Surface. Writing them for the occasion is the authored-criteria failure Tier 1 exists to avoid.
- THE PREVIOUS MEASUREMENT OF THIS FIXTURE IS WITHDRAWN, NOT SUPERSEDED (see Withdrawn): it reported v1 0.8 / approve 1/3 / NOT met, and every point of that was HD-004 — a second frontmatter parser that discarded YAML block lists, emptying use_case_refs, touched_files, depends_on and unlocks on all twenty tasks. approve_at also moved 0.85 -> 1.0 in this fixture, and that is a correction rather than a tuning: GATE L1b's own condition is spec-lint red == 0, so every structural row passing IS the gate's bar.

### `scope-architect`

- MEASURED 2026-08-04 on claude-sonnet-5, n=3, fixture 9b664b53b5896f58 (the EXTERNAL-FACT fixture): v1 0.944 [0.833, 1] -> final 1.0, delta +0.056, improved 1/3, approve 3/3, and ONE OF THREE RUNS NEEDED A SECOND ROUND. $4.7643.
- THE SECOND SKILL EVER TO MEET CONDITION 4, and it took a third escalation dial to get there. Dial one (complexity of one artifact) and dial two (volume of mutually-consistent constraints) both left this skill at 1.0 on the first draft, 3/3 — and the dial-two escalation demonstrably landed, since one first draft produced seven cap-compliant disjoint scopes over twenty tasks. What moved it was making one row depend on a fact OUTSIDE the artifact: `e2e_verification_fixtures` are COMMANDS, and whether a command runs is a property of the build the model must go and check.
- WHAT THE REVISION ACTUALLY FIXED, from the stored artifacts: run 2's first draft declared every fixture as `TODO_STORE=<seeded-3-item-store.json> node src/cli/main.js …` — an angle-bracket PLACEHOLDER, which the shell then tried to open as a file. That is a fixture nobody ran, which is precisely the failure the row exists to catch; the revision round stripped the placeholder and every command ran green. The board also carries two features that are NOT BUILT (tag/untag, export) against a CLI that implements six commands, and all three runs correctly wrote TBD there rather than inventing a fixture — SKILL.md's own rule.
- THE ROW DELEGATES TO t0-verify's OWN RUNNER (`runFixtures`), so a fixture is graded exactly as GATE L2 will grade it — `shell: true`, pass iff exit 0 — rather than by a second runner that would drift from it. This is the same principle the rest of this file follows: a second implementation of a rule is a second rule.
- THREE APPARATUS CORRECTIONS WERE MADE BEFORE THIS NUMBER EXISTED, and a run was KILLED rather than published to make them. The probe had run against an empty store (failing `done 1` environmentally); HD-002 shredded a quoted TBD note into four bogus commands; HD-003 discarded a YAML block sequence whole. Re-scored under the corrected instrument, that killed run's first drafts read 6/6 and 5/6 — one had been RIGHT ALL ALONG and was marked down by the parser. Publishing it would have reported the harness as skill quality, which is the withdrawn -0.571 measurement's exact shape.
- THREE OF SIX ROWS ARE AUTHORED (SA-PRESENT, SA-COVERAGE, SA-FIXTURES) and each is named as such here. SA-FIXTURES' criterion is SKILL.md's own sentence — 'too speculative to fixture -> mark TBD and flag it, never invent a fixture for unbuilt behavior'.
- Superseded fixtures 07ada0972c53b162 (original) and 9366adeec1f797f5 (the scale escalation) are retained; none of the three are a before/after of the skill.

### `solution-architect`

- MEASURED 2026-08-04 on claude-sonnet-5, n=3, fixture 552554ed2fc9d53e: v1 0.667 [0, 1] -> final 1.0, delta +0.333, improved 1/3, approve 3/3, and ONE OF THREE RUNS NEEDED A SECOND ROUND. $1.2955. Re-measured because the HD-001 fix changed contract-md.mjs and trace-lint.mjs, both of which this fixture grades through.
- THE FIRST SKILL WHOSE REVISION STEP EVER EXECUTED, and the most reproducible of the three that now do: reproduced across THREE independent measurements on three instrument versions (48943f1ee789b6e9 improved 1/3, 8bfbe80b203aeecd improved 2/3, 552554ed2fc9d53e improved 1/3), so it is a property of the task rather than a lucky sample. It is also the only one of the three whose approve_at (0.9) was never touched, so its verdict depends on no bar that moved.
- WHAT THE ROUNDS ACTUALLY FIXED, from the stored artifacts: run 1 and run 3 wrote six correct wiring entries under `# Wiring map — todo-cli` instead of the `## Wiring` heading contract-md.mjs keys the table on, so the map parsed as zero rows; the revision round moved the table under the right heading. These are CONFORMANCE defects, not reasoning defects. The loop demonstrably moved a real score by acting on a criterion-level defect, which is what Table II asks for; it did NOT demonstrate that the skill reasoned better on the second pass. Both are true and only the first is being claimed.
- THE FIXTURE WAS NOT CHANGED AFTER SEEING WHICH ROWS FAILED. Two failure modes looked like apparatus artifacts — the heading, and an engine cell written as `src/capture/add.js (`addTodo`)` rather than a bare path. The plan's §0 derivability audit rules against a fixture change on both: the heading is stated in the fixture prompt, and the bare path is stated in the skill's own SKILL.md ('repo-relative path — name the real path'). Rewriting a prompt after seeing the failures is the retuning §7.1 forbids, and the rule is only worth having if it also rules against changes the author wants to make.
- THE INSTRUMENT WAS CHANGED, and that is why there are two numbers. The first measurement of this fixture (48943f1ee789b6e9, retained under `superseded`) read v1 0.611 -> final 0.667, delta +0.056, approve 2/3. WM-REACH used to exclude engines whose path did not resolve — so it reported 'all 6 engines reach the entry point' for a map in which SIX OF SIX had never been resolved. A green row whose own evidence described nothing. The fix makes the row stricter and the measured result got BETTER, because the lenient version had been handing a half-passing round-1 draft 0.833 and letting a run stop early. The two numbers are not a before/after of the SKILL and must not be subtracted.
- THIS EVAL FOUND A PRODUCTION DEFECT, filed as HD-001 in shapeup/knowledge-base/harness-defects.md. trace-lint reports GREEN — 'reachability: 0/0 engines reach src/cli/main.js' — for a wiring-map.md holding six correct entries under an unrecognised heading. In a real run the artifact whose entire purpose is 'no engine ships orphaned' fails OPEN: the map is written, reviewed, committed, and the gate checks nothing. Reproduced deterministically, no model involved.

### `spec-evaluator`

- MEASURED 2026-08-04 on claude-sonnet-5, n=3, fixture 748827ec3dddd3a7: v1 1.0 -> final 1.0, delta 0, improved 0/3, approve 3/3, ONE round in every run. $2.4696.
- CEILINGED THROUGH ALL THREE DIALS, and the third one is the informative failure. JV-REPRO grades whether every bugs[].repro is a command that ACTUALLY RUNS — the same shape that moved solution-architect and scope-architect. It did not move this skill, and the stored drafts show why: all three runs wrote genuinely executable repros that seed their own store first, e.g. `printf '[{"text":"a",...}]' > /tmp/todo_ts06_repro.json; TODO_STORE=/tmp/todo_ts06_repro.json node build/todo.mjs rm 2-3`. Heredocs, store seeding, exit-code echoes. These are commands that were run, not descriptions that look like commands.
- THAT REFINES THE HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN CONTRADICTING IT. Dial three produces headroom where checking the external fact is OPTIONAL to producing a plausible artifact. For every other Tier-1 skill, checking is a step it may skip; for this one, checking IS THE JOB — 'absence of evidence = FAIL' is its first rule. A skill whose entire craft is verification does not skip verification, so the dial has nothing to catch here. The ceiling is a property of the task, and it is the right answer rather than a missing one.
- NINE AUTHORED CRITERIA DOWN TO THREE (now four with JV-REPRO, of twelve rows). A verdict is right or wrong only relative to what the build does, so verdict-rows.mjs runs the process oracle for GROUND TRUTH and grades AGREEMENT — one row per Test-Surface row. A FALSE-FAIL COSTS EXACTLY WHAT A FALSE-PASS COSTS, which nine must/must_not criteria written around one known planted bug could never do.
- THE TWO PLANTED DEFECTS ARE BOTH CAUGHT, first draft, every run — including TS-06, which is reachable ONLY against a seeded four-item store and which the build's own green suite cannot reach because every case in it runs on a fresh install. One run's evidence diagnosed the trap rather than just the bug: 'reachable only with a seeded 4+ item store, which is why the build's own suite (no seeded store) stays green'.
- JV-REPRO's POLARITY WAS CORRECTED BEFORE THE RUN, not after: the first version required a NON-ZERO exit, which would have failed exactly the defects it was written for — for a bug of the form 'should refuse and does not', exiting 0 IS the demonstration. The hand-authored strong reference caught it by failing its own row.

### `task-executor`

- MEASURED 2026-08-04 on claude-sonnet-5, n=3, fixture a864ec2ab81943f6 (the BROWNFIELD external-fact fixture): v1 1.0 -> final 1.0, delta 0, improved 0/3, approve 3/3, ONE round in every run. $1.5833.
- THE ONLY SKILL TO SURVIVE ALL THREE DIALS. Dial one twice (six contract rows, then twelve with batch selectors) and now dial three: the fixture hands over a WORKING CLI whose store is an envelope {v:1,items:[...]} known only to src/store/json-store.js, asks for one new command, and grades six REGRESSION rows over the commands that already worked. A `tag` written against the plain-array shape its neighbouring modules pass around looks entirely correct and takes four regressions down with it — the committed WEAK reference does exactly that and scores 0.4.
- IT HELD ON MERIT, NOT VACUOUSLY, and that was checked in the stored artifact rather than assumed: run 1's first draft imported `read`/`write` from json-store.js, left the envelope module untouched, and reused the existing `resolveSelectors` instead of writing its own. It went and read the file the answer was in.
- THIS IS A BROWNFIELD FIXTURE — the deliverable is seeded, so four structural guards written for greenfield deliverables were restated rather than dropped: §48(d1b) now asserts the handed-in baseline scores BELOW min_strong (there is real work in the fixture) instead of exactly 0; §48(d6) asserts round 1 starts from the seed and is not marked carried_forward; and P1's two prompt guards ($TODO_STORE, the store format) apply only to fixtures that do NOT seed the interface, because when the implementation is handed over the convention is derivable by reading it and restating it in the prompt would hand over the answer to the one row that measures whether the skill reads before writing. Mutation-verified: making the seeded baseline clear min_strong fires the new guard.
- A do-nothing build scores 0.6 because regressions are preserved by changing nothing. That is honest arithmetic for a regression contract, not a soft floor — and the empty draft still scores 0, because there is no deliverable to run.

## Limitations of the instrument

- SCORING IS DETERMINISTIC, NOT A MODEL JUDGE. Four of the five rubrics delegate every row to a script that already grades the artifact (spec-lint, trace-lint, board-derive, the process oracle); the fifth (task-executor) delegates all twelve. No model judge is involved anywhere in Tier 1, deliberately — a judge head would re-introduce the authorship this tier exists to remove.
- THREE ESCALATION DIALS WERE TESTED ACROSS ELEVEN PAID MEASUREMENTS, AND ONLY THE THIRD PRODUCES HEADROOM. Dial one, COMPLEXITY of a single artifact (task-executor 6 contract rows -> 12 with batch selectors; spec-evaluator a second planted bug reachable only by a seeded probe): no movement. Dial two, VOLUME of mutually-consistent constraints (ba-pitch-analyzer 9 tasks/8 edges -> 20 tasks/36 edges; scope-architect 17 files/8 tasks -> 36 files/20 tasks against a cap forcing a five-way split): no movement, and the escalations demonstrably landed — one first draft computed a 27-edge inverse map correctly, another produced seven cap-compliant disjoint scopes covering twenty tasks. Dial three, AGREEMENT WITH A FACT OUTSIDE THE ARTIFACT: three of the five skills now revise. Every fixture named here ships a committed PARTIAL reference scoring strictly between its weak and strong ones, so none of these ranges are notional.
- THE REFINED HYPOTHESIS, WHICH THE TWO REMAINING CEILINGS SUPPORT RATHER THAN CONTRADICT: dial three produces headroom where checking the external fact is OPTIONAL to producing a plausible artifact AND the model actually skips it. solution-architect named engines it had not traced to the entry point; scope-architect declared a fixture command it had never run; ba-pitch-analyzer named module paths it had not looked up. The two that held did the checking anyway — spec-evaluator wrote repro commands with heredocs and store seeding because verification IS its craft, and task-executor opened json-store.js before writing against the store, which was verified in its stored artifact rather than assumed. Two skipped, two did not; the dial predicts which, and 'the model checked' is a result about the skill, not a fixture that failed.
- ONE OF THE THREE 'MET' VERDICTS IS DOWNSTREAM OF A BAR I MOVED, and it must be read that way. ba-pitch-analyzer's three first drafts scored 0.9, 1.0, 1.0. Under the fixture's original approve_at of 0.85 all three would have approved on round 1, the loop would never have revised, and the row would read 'exit criterion only'. I raised approve_at to 1.0 when the external-fact row was added, and the justification is real and was written down before the run — GATE L1b's own condition is spec-lint red == 0, so every structural row passing IS the gate's bar, and 0.85 had been set when the rubric had nine rows and no external-fact row. But the causal chain is what it is: THE BAR CHANGE IS WHAT PRODUCED THAT MET. scope-architect's approve_at was 1.0 from the fixture's creation, before any measurement, so its verdict does not depend on a bar that moved; solution-architect's is 0.9 and unchanged throughout.
- THE PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION WAS WRONG, AND THE HYPOTHESIS WAS REFINED AFTER SEEING THE RESULT — which is exactly the shape of a post-hoc rescue, so it is flagged rather than smoothed. Before spec-evaluator and task-executor were measured under dial three, this baseline recorded the prediction that they WOULD show headroom because their graded rows would depend on a fact they had to verify. Both held at 1.0, 3/3. The refinement — that the fact must be optional to plausibility AND the model must actually skip checking it — explains the two ceilings, but it was formulated AFTER they were observed and it has not been tested against anything since. Read the dial-three finding as EXPLORATORY INSTRUMENT DESIGN, not as a confirmed mechanism: the hypothesis was formed after dials one and two failed, tested on skills whose fixtures were being rewritten at the same time, and has no held-out case. A confirmatory test would fix the recipe, apply it to a skill or fixture that played no part in forming it, and predict the outcome in writing beforehand.
- TWELVE SUPERSEDED FIXTURES FOR FIVE SKILLS IN ONE DAY. Every change is declared and both numbers are published, which is what §7.1 requires — but the RATE is its own caveat. The stopping condition for fixture iteration was, in practice, 'did a revision round happen', and iterating an instrument until it produces the movement you are looking for is adjacent to tuning it toward the answer. Two things argue against that reading and neither is conclusive: each change had a stated hypothesis written before the run rather than after the failure, and every fixture ships a committed PARTIAL reference proving its range is real. The honest summary is that these five numbers describe fixtures that were designed today, by one author, to be capable of showing a revision — and that they succeeded at that says less about the skills than the table's three MET verdicts make it look.
- WHAT EVERY REVISION ACTUALLY FIXED WAS CONFORMANCE OR DILIGENCE, NOT REASONING — all three of them, and the headline should be read through this. solution-architect: a markdown table under the wrong heading. scope-architect: an angle-bracket placeholder in a command nobody had run. ba-pitch-analyzer: module paths that are not on disk, plus `UC-01.md` where the lint resolves `UC-01`. The loop demonstrably moved real scores by acting on criterion-level defects, which is what Table II asks for and what this repo had never shown. It did NOT show any skill reasoning better on the second pass, and no number here supports that claim. The deltas are also small in two of the three cases (+0.033 and +0.056) and each rests on ONE run of three.
- EXIT CRITERION IS `final_score >= approve_at`, not `delta > 0`. Under the old delta rule a perfect 3/3 run reads 'NOT met' — the criterion penalised a skill that was already right. Changed with explicit operator authorisation after the flaw was measured, not quietly. The `revised?` column carries what the delta rule used to, and is what distinguishes MET from `exit criterion only`.
- VACUOUS TRUTH IS THE HAZARD SPECIFIC TO A LINT-DELEGATED RUBRIC, and one instance shipped before being caught. A lint reports no finding for an artifact that does not exist, so 'no PA1 violation' is trivially true of an empty scopes/ directory. Every row renderer now fails ALL of its rows when the artifact it grades is absent, and structural §48(d1b) asserts a seed-only workspace scores exactly 0. The instance that got through: WM-REACH excluded unresolvable engines and reported 'all 6 engines reach the entry point' for a map where six of six had never resolved. Caught only because a paid run produced a green row whose own evidence described nothing.
- SCOPE OF EVERY NUMBER HERE: n=3 loops per skill, ONE fixture per skill, 5 of 13 skills instrumented (the honest ceiling is 6 of 13 — five Tier-1 plus translator), and every live number is claude-sonnet-5. A quality rate is MODEL-dependent AND FIXTURE-dependent: task-executor's fixture has been replaced twice and spec-evaluator's once, and no number here generalises to the skill's behaviour on other work or on another model.
- THE MEASUREMENT FOUND FOUR PRODUCTION DEFECTS AND THAT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE SCORES. All four are one family — the committed contract format FAILS SILENT — and all four surfaced because a real worker wrote a real committed artifact and a real gate read it. HD-001: a table under an unrecognised heading parses empty, and trace-lint then reports green '0/0 engines reach' for a wiring map holding six correct rows. HD-002: a quoted list member was split on its own commas, turning a worker's honest TBD note into four bogus entries on a field t0-verify EXECUTES. HD-003/HD-004: a YAML block sequence was discarded whole — and the repo turned out to have TWO hand-rolled parsers for one documented format, so fixing the first left the second silently returning empty and cost a full paid measurement. All four are fixed, pinned by structural §46(f)(g)(h), and mutation-verified. THE PATTERN MATTERS MORE THAN THE BUGS: every one of them first appeared as a SKILL scoring badly. An eval not instrumented to tell harness failure from skill failure will under-report skill quality and read as a confident measurement while doing it — four instances in one day, on a harness that was already unusually careful about this.

## Retired measurements

These were measured **correctly**. What changed was the instrument or the publishing
policy, not the finding — so they are kept beside the current numbers rather than replaced
by them. Two causes, and they mean different things:

- **fixture-change** — the prompt, seeded spec or oracle contract moved underneath a valid
  measurement. The successor fingerprint is named. The two numbers are **not** a
  before/after of the skill and must not be subtracted.
- **model-policy** — the number was right and is simply no longer the model this repo
  publishes. No fixture changed, so no successor fingerprint exists to name.

## Withdrawn measurements

Kept rather than deleted: a number that was published and retracted is evidence about the
instrument, and removing it silently is how a fabricated baseline survives.

- **— / claude-haiku-4-5-20251001** (2026-08-03) — reported {"delta_mean":0.024,"improved_runs":"1/3","final_mean":0.095,"verdict":"NOT met"}.
  <br/>Withdrawn: PROXY ARTIFACT — not a measurement of skill quality. The headless adapter ran at --max-turns 12; the CLI exhausted the budget and printed `Error: Reached max turns (12)` (29 bytes) on stdout with exit 0. The adapter's broken-harness guard only rejected EMPTY output, so that error string was scored against the rubric as if it were the model's draft. An independent run on claude-sonnet-5 produced a byte-identical 29-byte draft, confirming the cause is the harness and not the model. Withdrawn, not carried forward — the same disposition the prior trigger-eval TPR was given (audit F1).
- **— / claude-haiku-4-5-20251001** (2026-08-03) — reported {"v1":0.571,"final":0,"delta":-0.571,"verdict":"NOT met"}.
  <br/>Withdrawn: PERMISSION-BLOCKED — the delta is an artifact, not skill quality. The headless probe ran with no permission grant, so the skill could not execute `node` to probe the running build. Its round-3 reply was verbatim: 'I need permission to run the Node.js process to probe the build.' That is CORRECT behaviour — it refused to fabricate an observation it could not make — and it scores 0, so a 0.571 first draft 'regressed' to 0. Compounded by the revision prompt not demanding a complete artifact, so the model answered with a plan instead of a report. NOTE: v1=0.571 is itself a valid first-draft score; only the DELTA is invalid.
- **ba-pitch-analyzer / claude-sonnet-5** (2026-08-04) — reported {"v1_mean":0.8,"final_mean":0.867,"delta_mean":0.067,"improved_runs":"1/3","approved_runs":"1/3","verdict":"NOT met"}.
  <br/>Withdrawn: HD-004 — NOT a measurement of skill quality. All three runs wrote task frontmatter as YAML BLOCK SEQUENCES, and board-derive.mjs's private `listField` read only the inline `[a, b]` form. Every list field on every task therefore came back EMPTY: `use_case_refs` (so UC-ANCHOR went red for all of them), `touched_files` (so the external-fact row reported 'none did'), and `depends_on`/`unlocks` — the last pair empty in BOTH directions, so edge-symmetry passed VACUOUSLY. This is the second instance of HD-003: the same defect had just been fixed in contract-md.mjs, and the repo turned out to have a SECOND hand-rolled frontmatter parser for the same documented format. Re-scored under the fix, the identical stored drafts read 9/10, 9/10 and 10/10 rather than 8/10 across the board. A second, smaller apparatus fault rode along: the fixture prompt said use_case_refs must 'match a use-case FILENAME' while its own example showed the bare id, and all three runs wrote `UC-01.md`, which is the filename and which the lint does not resolve. Withdrawn rather than superseded because the number describes the harness, not the skill — the same disposition the max-turns and permission-denial artifacts were given. Successor: fixture e275807eff45902b.

## What remains

Tier 1 is 5 skills (`task-executor`, `scope-architect`, `solution-architect`, `ba-pitch-analyzer`, `spec-evaluator`).

| Item | Skills | State |
|---|---|---|
| No rubric yet | — | 0 of 5 Tier-1 skills unbuilt |
| Rubric built, never measured | — | needs an authenticated `--measure` |
| Measured but **ceilinged** — approves on the first draft, so the revision step has never run | `spec-evaluator`, `task-executor` | needs a harder fixture, not a new rubric |

A skill counts as done for this rung when its loop **revises** — a first draft below the bar,
a revision round that acts on criterion-level defects, and a final score that clears it. A
rubric that approves round 1 every time is a pass/fail check wearing a loop's clothes.

## Method

tools/skill-loop.mjs --measure (reflective_task per Graph Engineering §VI.A): round 1 is the skill's first draft, each later round re-prompts with the criterion-level failures from the rubric's DETERMINISTIC head; stopping rule = score >= that fixture's approve_at, or 5 rounds. Each round is one headless session at --max-turns 50, granted Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep/Bash — the shell is part of the measured configuration because task-executor uses one to run its own T0 probes in production, and a session denied it aborts rather than producing a number. n=3 independent loops per skill. The graded artifact is the DELIVERABLE FILE, not the transcript, and each revision round starts from the previous round's deliverable in a fresh directory — so a round edits one artifact rather than re-drawing it. Runs before 2026-08-04 did NOT carry it forward and are re-sampling, not revision; they are not comparable on delta. Oracle criteria are scored per ROW (fraction of contract rows passing), not all-or-nothing; `satisfied` still requires every row, so approve_at is unchanged in meaning. Runs before 2026-08-04 scored these criteria binary and recorded 0.0 for any artifact short of perfect. Quality rates are MODEL-DEPENDENT — this baseline describes the model named below and no other. EVERY Tier-1 row is scored by an ORACLE, never by a regex over prose and never by a model judge: the rubrics delegate to spec-lint, trace-lint, board-derive and the process oracle, which were written before this measurement existed. The stopping rule is per-fixture (approve_at 0.9 for solution-architect, 1.0 for the rest) — the report's `approve` column is against each fixture's own bar.

**Adapter:** default: claude --plugin-dir <root> -p <prompt>

**Reproduce:** `node tools/skill-loop.mjs --measure --skill <name> --model claude-sonnet-5`
